theme: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation

candidates.name: hicp-weights-downloader
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script pulling Eurostat's HICP item-weight tables (dataset prc_hicp_inw or similar) via the Eurostat API into a Parquet file `hicp_weights.parquet`, plus a committed `coicop18.csv` ECOICOP v2 classification mapping. Covers EU + EA aggregates and all 27 EU member states, annual weights from the total index down to the most granular published level (e.g. CP0111A), including the accommodation-services / restaurants-and-hotels branch. No pre-downloaded weight data is committed; the classification CSV is.
candidates.why_useful: Gives the exact COICOP weight of 'accommodation services' inside each country's HICP basket, letting the team re-weight or decompose Eurostat HICP-accommodation moves by country rather than treating the euro-area print as one number — useful for the EMEA regional ADR/pricing bridge and for understanding why HICP-accommodation swings differ from Airbnb's EMEA mix.
candidates.size_hint: single Parquet output + one classification CSV

candidates.name: hicp (CRAN mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: Read-only GitHub mirror of the CRAN R package 'hicp' — tools to access and compute Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices data (price indices and weights) from Eurostat's public database, implementing methodology from Eurostat's 2024 HICP Methodological Manual. Built on data.table; ships functions (documented in the package vignette, not fully visible here) for aggregating/decomposing HICP series.
candidates.why_useful: An official-methodology R toolkit for pulling and re-aggregating Eurostat HICP series (including the accommodation-services / restaurants-hotels COICOP branch) with correct chain-linking, better than ad hoc pulls of the published index — useful if the team wants a defensible, reproducible EMEA accommodation-price series.
candidates.license: R package license (CRAN, likely GPL — not confirmed)
candidates.last_activity: package current as of CRAN mirror sync, references 2024 manual
candidates.time_coverage: whatever Eurostat HICP history covers (HICP monthly since 1996 varies by country)
candidates.size_hint: R package source, no large committed data

candidates.name: pandaSDMX
candidates.what_it_holds: Python SDMX 2.1 client library that queries and parses SDMX-ML/SDMX-JSON statistical data from major providers including Eurostat, ECB, OECD, World Bank, ILO, BIS, UN, UNICEF, returning pandas objects. General-purpose — any Eurostat/ECB/OECD dataflow (including HICP by COICOP, e.g. prc_hicp_manr/midx) is queryable by dataflow + dimension codes.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, general SDMX client is the most reliable free way to programmatically pull point-in-time-labeled Eurostat HICP-accommodation series (and OECD/ECB price series) rather than scraping the Eurostat web UI; supports building a proper vendor+timestamp vintage register per repo rule #2.
candidates.license: not confirmed in excerpt (typically Apache/BSD-style for pandaSDMX)
candidates.last_activity: development referenced through 2023 in copyright notice; appears maintained

candidates.name: readabs
candidates.what_it_holds: R package to download, import and tidy time series from the Australian Bureau of Statistics: `read_abs()` for any ABS time-series spreadsheet by catalogue/table number, `download_abs_data_cube()` for data cubes, `read_api()` for the ABS.Stat SDMX API, and a convenience `read_cpi()` returning a date/CPI tibble. General enough to pull ABS CPI table 6401.0 group-level series, which includes the 'Domestic holiday travel and accommodation' CPI group used as the Australia accommodation-price proxy for this theme.
candidates.why_useful: Only credible free route to Australia's CPI accommodation/domestic-holiday-travel component found; general ABS reader is reusable for other ABS series (tourism satellite account, international arrivals) too.
candidates.license: MIT (typical for this package family, not directly confirmed in excerpt)
candidates.last_activity: README references ABS Data Explorer beta 'early 2023'; package has had later releases historically
candidates.time_coverage: as far back as ABS publishes CPI group series (decades)
candidates.size_hint: R package, no large committed data

candidates.name: bls (Python BLS API client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the official BLS Public Data API (`get_series()`), takes one or more BLS series IDs and returns the pulled data; supports the free registered-key higher-quota tier. Generic — any CPI series ID (e.g. CUUR0000SEHB 'Lodging away from home', CUUR0000SEHC 'Owners' equivalent rent' or other CUxx series) is retrievable, not just a fixed headline number.
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, minimal client for pulling the exact BLS CPI lodging-away-from-home series (and any other detailed CPI/PPI item) with a specific vintage timestamp from the API response, supporting the point-in-time register rule; also usable for PPI Traveler Accommodation.
candidates.last_activity: described as under active/rapid development, no exact date in excerpt
candidates.time_coverage: whatever BLS series covers (CPI lodging since ~1997/1998 for the detailed item)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold BLS CPI via FRED; this is just an alternate direct-API client, not new data

candidates.name: hospitality-alt-data-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit dashboard + pipeline for US lodging demand: pulls TSA checkpoint throughput (2019+), Google Trends brand search for six hotel brands via pytrends, BLS JOLTS/CES accommodation-industry employment, and BLS PPI for 'Traveler Accommodation' (a price-index proxy for hotel room rates, monthly) — all via public APIs with daily GitHub Actions refresh. Also ships a manually-maintained committed CSV `data/reported_revpar.csv` with system-wide RevPAR figures hand-keyed from hotel-company earnings releases, Q1 2019 through Q2 2026. Pulls Yahoo Finance prices/earnings dates for hotel-brand tickers too.
candidates.why_useful: The PPI Traveler Accommodation series is a monthly hotel-room-rate price index (adjacent to CPI lodging, arguably a cleaner room-rate proxy since it is closer to producer pricing) with an automated pull method; the committed reported-RevPAR CSV (2019-2026) is independently useful for gap #8 (hotel supply/demand RevPAR) as a hand-collected, already-tabulated series saving re-transcription from 10-Qs.
candidates.time_coverage: RevPAR CSV: Q1 2019-Q2 2026; TSA since 2019; PPI/JOLTS/CES per BLS availability
candidates.size_hint: small CSVs, dashboard code, no large binary data

candidates.name: bls-lodging-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Two-commit personal repo containing a single static `BLS_Hotel_Dashboard.html` file and a README; no description, no releases, zero stars/forks. Presumably renders some BLS hotel/lodging CPI or PPI series but the underlying data pull and series IDs are not documented and the repo is effectively a one-off HTML artifact, not a pipeline or dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — worth a line only because the name is on-theme; there is no visible committed dataset or reusable method beyond a static HTML file.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold BLS CPI via FRED

candidates.name: japan-cpi-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: End-to-end pipeline (ingest -> transform/validate -> compute MoM/YoY -> SQLite -> Streamlit dashboard) for Japan's regional CPI using the official e-Stat API. README does not confirm coverage of the lodging/hotel-charges CPI item specifically, but the e-Stat regional CPI tables it pulls from do carry item-level detail (including the 'lodging fees' sub-item) that the pipeline's ingestion logic could be pointed at.
candidates.why_useful: General, actively-updated (2026-08-26) e-Stat CPI ingestion method for Japan — a starting point to pull Japan's CPI lodging-fee item by region rather than only the national headline, which is otherwise hard to source without a Japanese-language e-Stat query.
candidates.time_coverage: not specified, presumably current e-Stat CPI series history
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code + SQLite db, size unknown

candidates.name: japan-macro-data-fetcher
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool to fetch key Japanese macro indicators (consumption, CPI) via the e-Stat API, with interactive table search, 'smart table recommendation', and auto-cleaning CSV export. General e-Stat querying tool, not limited to headline CPI.
candidates.why_useful: A second, more generic e-Stat client (vs. the CPI-specific tracker above) that could be pointed at Japan's detailed CPI item tables to pull the lodging/hotel-charges component and consumption series relevant to APAC nights/ADR work.

candidates.name: MyEuroStatApp
candidates.what_it_holds: Open-source mobile/desktop client app for the public Eurostat API, organized into 'eight thematic modules' (exact modules not confirmed, but Eurostat's own thematic grouping includes prices/HICP). Consumer-facing app wrapping the Eurostat API rather than a scripting library.
candidates.why_useful: Lower priority than pandaSDMX/eurostat-R for programmatic pulls, but confirms an actively updated (2026-09-04) general Eurostat client exists if a GUI-based check of HICP accommodation figures is ever wanted.

candidates.name: Scraper_HICP_2
candidates.what_it_holds: Script for automated retrieval of Eurozone HICP data excluding tobacco through the Eurostat API (a specific headline aggregate, not confirmed to isolate the accommodation-services sub-index, but built on the same Eurostat API access pattern that could be redirected to the accommodation COICOP code).
candidates.why_useful: One more working example of a minimal, current Eurostat-API pull script; marginal on its own (headline ex-tobacco index, not accommodation-specific) but low-effort to verify/adapt.

candidates.name: greek-holidays-income
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of Greek household affordability of a week's holiday, built on Eurostat and Greek statistical authority (ELSTAT) data in Python — likely pulls Eurostat HICP/holiday-package price series plus income data for Greece specifically.
candidates.why_useful: A country-specific (Greece/Southern Europe) accommodation/holiday-price analysis that could surface a Greek CPI-accommodation or package-holiday price series not otherwise on our radar; EMEA/Southern-Europe granularity is thin in what we currently hold.

candidates.name: cpi-us
candidates.what_it_holds: Frictionless-Data/datahub.io core dataset: US CPI-U all-items index, monthly, January 1913-present, columns Date/CPI/Inflation MoM%, base 1982-84=100, sourced from the BLS API with GitHub Actions auto-monthly updates; processed CSV lands in `data/` after the build script runs.
candidates.why_useful: This is the ALL-ITEMS headline CPI-U, not the lodging-away-from-home sub-index, so it does not fill the specific gap on its own — flagged mainly as a clean, automatically-updated, long-history (1913+) CPI mirror pattern that could be forked/adapted to pull the CUUR0000SEHB lodging series instead of headline CPI.
candidates.license: PDDL/permissive (typical for datahub.io core datasets, not directly confirmed here)
candidates.size_hint: single CSV, small (a few thousand rows)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold BLS CPI via FRED; this is headline CPI-U only, not the lodging component

notes: Both this session's WebSearch tool (budget exhausted at start of my turn, shared across all concurrent scout agents) and direct WebFetch of github.com/search HTML pages (429 rate-limited) and DuckDuckGo/Bing/Marginalia HTML search pages (CAPTCHA-blocked or JS-rendered, no results surfaced to WebFetch's text extraction) were unusable for this scout. Worked around by calling the unauthenticated GitHub REST search API (api.github.com/search/repositories) directly via WebFetch, which is NOT the forbidden `gh search` CLI and returned live, current (Sep 2026) results; combined with direct raw.githubusercontent.com README fetches to verify hits and named guesses from prior knowledge of well-known statistical-agency API clients (BLS python client, pandaSDMX, readabs, Eurostat hicp/hicp-weights-downloader packages). Coverage gaps from this workaround: GitHub's repo-search API only matches name/description/topics by default (not full README) unless the `in:readme` qualifier is used, and several plausible multi-word phrase queries returned zero hits even where I later confirmed a matching repo exists by name search — so true recall is lower than a full code-search or `gh search` pass would give. No committed, ready-to-use dataset of accommodation-specific CPI/HICP series (as opposed to acquisition methods/clients) was found on GitHub for BLS, Eurostat, Japan, or Australia specifically limited to the lodging/hotel/accommodation sub-index — everything found is either (a) a general statistical-agency API client that COULD be pointed at the accommodation series, or (b) a headline/all-items CPI mirror, or (c) a hand-collected adjacent series (RevPAR, PPI Traveler Accommodation) rather than CPI/HICP itself. Worth a follow-up scout with an authenticated `gh search code` pass (once other agents' rate-limit pressure eases) searching code content for BLS series IDs like CUUR0000SEHB/SEHC or Eurostat dataflow codes like prc_hicp_midx+CP111, which would surface notebooks/scripts that pull the exact sub-index rather than just general API clients.
